name: HarborGrid Crane & Dock Supervisor Jacket
description: The Crane & Dock Supervisor Jacket is the distinguishing garment of anyone running a shift at GLMZ's lakefront cargo terminals — a role that involves managing automated crane systems, human crews, radiation-flagged cargo protocols, and the constant weather off Lake Michigan. The jacket is a heavyweight canvas-shell design with a Dyneema-reinforced outer layer and a removable thermal lining for the winter corridor season. High-visibility panels — retroreflective gold-orange — run along the shoulders and forearms, and a GPS-linked beacon chip is embedded in the right collar point, standard for anyone working in active crane swing zones. The HarborGrid Collective patch on the left arm indicates union seniority tier; supervisors have earned the gold-bordered version. Pockets include a sealed document pocket rated for spray exposure and a dedicated slot for the supervisor's radiation dosimeter clip.
cultural_context: The HarborGrid Collective is one of the few remaining worker-organized bodies with real negotiating power in GLMZ, and the jacket is a marker of that membership. Non-union dock workers wear different colors and are paid significantly less. The gold-bordered patch takes years to earn and is worn with visible pride. Corponation logistics managers who try to bypass the Collective's jurisdiction often find the jacket's wearers an unusually unified obstacle.
story_hooks: A supervisor's dosimeter has been showing elevated readings for three weeks but the cargo manifests for that dock show nothing radioactive — someone is moving something off the books through that terminal.
A recently deceased supervisor's jacket, gold-bordered patch and all, has been claimed by two different people, each with a credible story about how they came to have it.

The GPS beacon chips in a full shift's worth of supervisor jackets all went dark simultaneously during a four-hour window — and during that window, something moved through the terminal that doesn't appear in any cargo log.

physical_description.visual_profile: A robust, authoritative work jacket with military-industrial undertones. Broad shoulders with reinforced structure, slightly oversized through the torso for layering and movement. The retroreflective gold-orange panels create bold horizontal stripes across shoulders and forearms, making the wearer immediately visible in low-light dock environments. The silhouette reads as functional and assertive — a garment that commands presence.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the body with articulated sleeves for crane operation and cargo handling. Slightly tapered at the waist to avoid bulk. Designed to accommodate thermal liners without compression. Cuffs are fitted but not tight, allowing wrist augmentation interfaces to be visible if worn.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight Dyneema-reinforced ballistic canvas outer shell; brushed synthetic-wool blend thermal lining (removable); sealed synthetic leather on collar and cuff reinforcement panels
physical_description.texture: Rough, weathered canvas with a slight waxy finish from treatment. Dyneema weave creates subtle diagonal ribbing. Collar and reinforcement panels are smooth and worn with age. Gold-orange retroreflective panels have a subtle dimpled texture for light diffusion.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial charcoal-gray canvas base with bold gold-orange retroreflective horizontal stripes on shoulders and forearms. Black synthetic-leather collar and cuff trim. HarborGrid Collective patch features deep navy with gold border (supervisor tier), bright white embroidered lettering.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty YKK brass zipper down center front with reinforced storm flap. Magnetic snap collar closures for quick removal. Thermal lining attaches via friction-fit connectors at shoulder seams and waistband.
distinctive_features: GPS-linked beacon chip embedded in right collar point (subtle antenna visible as reinforced stitching)
HarborGrid Collective union patch on left chest with gold-bordered supervisor version
Sealed document pocket on right hip rated for water/spray exposure
Dedicated radiation dosimeter clip slot on right waist (permanently stitched retention loop)
Reinforced elbow and shoulder panels in darker charcoal with abrasion resistance
Inner collar embossed with wearer's shift authorization code (thermal-printed)
Radiation warning iconography subtly woven into interior pocket lining
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional; the gold-bordered patch elevates it to Tier 2 status within the working class, signaling earned authority and union protection
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this jacket means you belong to the HarborGrid Collective — one of GLMZ's last worker-organized power centers. The gold-bordered supervisor patch is a credential, not just decoration; it signals years of service, technical competence, and union seniority. Non-union dock workers view this jacket with a mix of envy and resentment. Corporate logistics managers recognize it as a warning: the wearer's first loyalty is to the Collective, not corpo directives.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly worn. Canvas shows stress creases from repeated wear, particularly around shoulders and elbows. The thermal lining may show minor separations at stress points. Retroreflective panels are dulled slightly from repeated dock spray and salt air exposure, but still functional. The HarborGrid patch shows proud wear; many supervisors have small memorial stitches or modified edges acknowledging lost crew members.
